points: Any player may call a service let, including the server. Call it right away.
A service let on a second serve means one more second serve.
A serve that hits the receiver or the receiver's partner before it bounces is the server's point.
Tossing and catching the ball is not a fault. Swinging and missing is a fault.
A delay between first and second serve: caused by the receiver or from outside, two serves. Caused by the server, one serve.
The receiver must play at the server's reasonable pace. If you are not ready, signal before the serve motion starts. If you try to return the serve, you were ready.
Foot faults: warn first. Call one only if it goes on and is clear from your side of the net.

questions.q: Who may call a service let?
options: Any player on the court, including the server
Only the receiver
Only the receiving team
Only the player closest to the net
questions.why: Any player may call a service let, including the server.

questions.q: The serve looks like an ace, but you heard it touch the net. When must you call the let?
options: At once
Any time before the next serve
At the end of the game
You cannot call a let on an ace
questions.why: Call a service let before the return goes out of play or is hit by the serving side. On an apparent ace, call it at once.

questions.q: Your second serve touches the net and lands in the right box. What happens?
options: You get one more second serve
You get two serves
It is a double fault
The serve is good and the point goes on
questions.why: A service let on a second serve means one more second serve.

questions.q: Your serve hits the receiver's partner at the net before it bounces. What is the call?
options: Your point
A fault
A let, serve again
Their point
questions.why: A serve that hits the receiver or the receiver's partner before bouncing gives the point to the server.

questions.q: You toss the ball, do not like the toss, and catch it. Is it a fault?
options: No. Toss again
Yes, it counts as a fault
Yes, if you catch it with your racket
No, but only once per game
questions.why: Tossing and catching the ball is not a fault. You may catch it with your hand or racket, or let it bounce.

questions.q: You toss the ball, swing, and miss it completely. What is the call?
options: A fault
No fault, the same as catching the toss
A let, serve again
A fault only on a second serve
questions.why: Missing the ball entirely when you swing at it is a fault.

questions.q: Your first serve looked long to you, but the receiver hit it back and made no call. Do you get to replay the point?
options: No. The serve was good and the point counts
Yes. Take your first serve again
Yes, but with a second serve
Yes, if your partner also saw it long
questions.why: If the receiver plays a serve you thought was out and does not call it, you do not get a replay.

questions.q: You miss your first serve. Before your second serve the receiver stops to tie a shoe, and you wait. How many serves do you get?
options: Two serves
One serve
One serve, and the receiver gets a warning
The receiver decides
questions.why: If the receiver or something from outside causes a delay between first and second serve, the server gets two serves.
questions.ref: Guide section 04, Delays between first and second serve

questions.q: You miss your first serve, then stop to dry your grip and fix your hat. How many serves do you get?
options: One serve
Two serves
Two serves, if the receiver agrees
None. It is a double fault
questions.why: If the server causes the delay, it is still one serve.
questions.ref: Guide section 04, Delays between first and second serve

questions.q: You miss your first serve. The ball stays near the net and someone quickly clears it. Do you get two serves?
options: Not for that alone. The receiver judges if the delay was long enough
Yes, always
Yes, if the server asks for it
No, never after a first serve fault
questions.why: Simply having to clear a stray ball between serves is not enough to earn two serves. The receiver judges whether the delay was long enough.
questions.ref: Guide section 04, Delays between first and second serve

questions.q: During your second serve motion, a ball from the next court rolls onto your court. What happens?
options: A let. The whole point is replayed, so you get two serves
A let. You take the second serve again
Play on. It is a fault if you miss
The receiver chooses one serve or two
questions.why: Something from outside coming onto the court during the second serve motion is a let. The whole point is replayed, so the server gets two serves.
questions.ref: Guide section 04, Delays between first and second serve

questions.q: You are receiving and you are not ready. When must you signal it?
options: Before the server starts the serve motion
Any time before the ball bounces
After the serve, by not swinging at it
At the next changeover
questions.why: If you are not ready, signal before the serve motion starts. Raise a hand while the server is still getting ready.

questions.q: You swing at a serve and miss. Then you say you were not ready. What is the call?
options: You were ready. Server's point
Replay the point
The server takes that serve again
A let, if your partner agrees
questions.why: A receiver who tries to return the serve is taken to be ready.

questions.q: As the receiver, how much time can you take to get ready for each serve?
options: You must play at the server's reasonable pace
As long as you need to feel set
Always the full 25 seconds
As long as your partner needs
questions.why: The server may not serve until you are ready, but you must play at the server's reasonable pace.

questions.q: You think your opponent is foot faulting. What must happen before you can call it?
options: You warn the server first, and it goes on in a way that is clear from your side
Nothing. You can call it the first time you see it
Your captain must see it too
Someone watching must confirm it
questions.why: The receiving side may call foot faults only after reasonable efforts such as a warning have failed, and the foot fault is clear from the receiver's side.

questions.q: You warned the server about foot faults. Now they step on the line by a hair, and you are not sure from your side. Can you call it?
options: No. If it is marginal, let it go
Yes, because you already warned them
Yes, if your partner thinks so too
Yes, but only on a second serve
questions.why: Even after a warning, a foot fault can be called only if it is so clear that you can see it from the receiver's side. A marginal one cannot be called.
